text: . Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei said today that the Strait of Hormuz will not reopen until the US continues its naval blockade against Iran. Addressing a weekly press briefing in Tehran, Baqaei said that the Strait of Hormuz was closed due to the US and Israeli military aggression against Iran. He emphasised that the reopening of the waterway relies on the conditions enforced on Iran and the Strait of Hormuz by the US and Israeli authorities. Baqaei mentioned that the talks between Iran and Oman over a shipping route is a bilateral matter which involves two nations. Earlier, Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Aragchi stated that there are currently no ongoing negotiations with the United States.

. Global crude oil prices edged higher today as Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei said that the Strait of Hormuz will not reopen until the US continues its naval blockade against Iran. Brent crude was trading 1.4 per cent up at 84 US dollars and 72 cents per barrel in intra-day trade. West Texas Intermediate crude was trading 1.1 per cent higher at 79 US dollars and two cents per barrel, when reports last came in.

. Minister of Tourism and Culture Gajendra Singh Shekhawat today said that cinema is more than entertainment; it is a bridge to culture, heritage and tourism. He said this during a fireside chat with Netflix Co-CEO Ted Sarandos in New Delhi. Mr Shekhawat highlighted that every Indian story has the potential to inspire someone, somewhere in the world, to experience India. The Minister said that India’s ancient civilisation and cultural diversity are its greatest strengths, and platforms like Netflix can play a key role in taking India’s stories and soft power to global audiences. He noted that the ministry’s partnership with Netflix, including the As Seen on Netflix integration on the Incredible India portal, reflects the shared vision of showcasing India’s rich cultural diversity and strengthening its global soft power through authentic storytelling. Mr Shekhawat also stressed that the Centre is working with all stakeholders to provide tourists with a seamless travel experience across the country.On the sidelines of the fireside chat, talking to Akashvani News, Mr  Shekhawat said that the Ministry’s partnerships with platforms such as Netflix, YouTube, Google, and airline companies including IndiGo and Air India are based on non-commercial and mutually beneficial agreements, without financial payments by the government to these companies.He said that these collaborations will promote India’s tourism globally by showcasing the country’s destinations and cultural diversity. The Minister highlighted that visual storytelling plays a crucial role in influencing travellers’ decisions.

. The Government has notified 11 more International Ports, enabling foreign nationals holding e-visas to enter India. The Home Ministry said the notification includes 9 land ports and 2 airports. These include airports at Bhopal and Tirupati and land ports at Attari and Agartala.The Ministry said the addition of these ports further enhances the attractiveness and utility of electronic visas. It noted that India processes approximately 95 per cent of e-visa applications in less than 72 hours. With the latest addition, the total number of International Ports enabling entry of foreign nationals holding e-visas has increased to 88, including 37 airports, 38 seaports and 13 land ports.

. Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju has said that  the government is ready for a detailed debate and reply on  the issue related to the  students’ protests. When the Lok Sabha reassembled after the second adjournment at 2 PM, Mr Rijiju said that Union Home Minister Amit Shah is ready to make a detailed  reply to the debate on the issue. He said, Congress and Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi were demanding a statement from the Home Minister on the issue. He urged the Congress and  other opposition parties to  listen to Home Minister’s reply peacefully and not  shy away from it.

. Minister of State for Petroleum and Natural Gas Suresh Gopi has informed that no decision has been taken by the Government to increase ethanol blending with petrol beyond 20 percent. In a written reply to a question in the Rajya Sabha, Mr Gopi said that any future decision regarding higher ethanol blends will be taken only after detailed scientific and technical studies and consultations with all relevant stakeholders, including automobile manufacturers and Oil Marketing Companies (OMCs).The Minister said that the Ethanol Blended Petrol (EBP) Programme has been implemented through a phased, scientifically validated and consultative process involving NITI Aayog, automobile manufacturers, OMCs  and technical institutions.He said, extensive laboratory studies and field trials covering parameters such as engine durability, emissions and fuel efficiency, have confirmed that E20 is safe for use under prescribed standards. The Minister added that these studies also established that legacy vehicles do not exhibit any significant variation in performance or abnormal wear and tear due to E20. The Minister said, these extensive laboratory studies, field validation and real-world operating experience have not established any widespread adverse impact on vehicle performance due to E20 fuel.

. India’s Ambassador to Israel, J.P. Singh, met the Head of MASHAV, Israel’s Agency for International Development Cooperation, Eynat Shlein, in Jerusalem to discuss ways to further expand and deepen the India-Israel development partnership through MASHAV. The discussions covered cooperation in several areas, including Centres of Excellence in agriculture, capacity building in agriculture and water management, and new avenues of cooperation in aquaculture. The Indian Embassy in Israel said the two sides also exchanged views on further strengthening the partnership.MASHAV, under Israel’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, was established to share Israeli knowledge, expertise and technologies with other countries to help them address development challenges.

. The 80th Independence Day celebrations this year will highlight Yuva Shakti and the contribution of young India towards building a Viksit Bharat by 2047, along with the commemoration of 150 years of the National Song, Vande Mataram. Briefing media in New Delhi today, Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh said, the celebrations will be led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi from the historic Red Fort. The Prime Minister will unfurl the National Flag and address the nation.A major highlight of this year’s celebrations will be the commemoration of 150 years of Vande Mataram. For the first time, the National Song will be sung from the ramparts of the Red Fort during the Independence Day ceremony. The ramparts will be decorated with floral arrangements based on the theme of Vande Mataram, while around 2 thousand 5 hundred NCC cadets and My Bharat volunteers will form a ‘Vande Mataram’ formation on Gyanpath. Vande Mataram will also be sung collectively at the Red Fort with Service bands, with everyone present standing at attention. Following the Prime Minister’s address, NCC cadets and My Bharat volunteers will sing the National Song, followed by the National Anthem.Mi-17 helicopters will participate in the ceremony, with the aerial display featuring the National Flag, flower petals and a special banner commemorating 150 years of Vande Mataram. As part of the nationwide celebrations, armed forces and other uniformed service bands will perform at 343 prominent locations from 8th to 15th of this month. Bands of the Army, Navy, Air Force, Coast Guard, NCC, CRPF, ITBP, CISF, SSB, BSF, IDS, RPF and Assam Rifles will participate.The second major theme of the celebration is ‘Yuva Shakti – Leading the Journey to Viksit Bharat@2047’. Nineteen medal-winning students from the 2026 International Physics, Chemistry, Biology and Mathematics Olympiads have been invited as special guests, along with young innovators, PM Internship Scheme interns, startups, PM Kaushal Vikas Yojana trainees, My Bharat volunteers and beneficiaries of various government schemes. Around 5 hundred Delhi government school students, selected through quizzes and competitions, will also attend the ceremony.The celebrations will also recognize other contributors to the Viksit Bharat vision, including women entrepreneurs supported under PM Mudra, PMAY-U beneficiaries, innovators and scientists, Bharat Taxi Sarthis, PM Surya Ghar beneficiaries, PM Vishwakarma artisans, PM Shram Yogi Maandhan beneficiaries, farmers and International Yoga Day volunteers.More than 15 hundred Delhi-based people representing different States and Union Territories and dressed in traditional attire have been invited. For invitees, Delhi Metro services will begin at 4 AM and will be free of cost. Around 2 hundred My Bharat and NCC volunteers will assist visitors, including those requiring wheelchair assistance. Cloakrooms, drinking water, toilets and rain ponchos will also be available, while parking locations will be provided through Google Maps and Mappls.After the ceremony, NCC cadets and My Bharat volunteers will undertake a Swachhata campaign at the Red Fort, focusing on systematic plogging and prompt removal of garbage.

. Parliament has passed the Bankers’ Books Evidence Bill, 2026, with the Rajya Sabha approving it today. Lok Sabha has already passed the Bill. Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman moved the Bill, which aims to modernise the legal framework to meet the requirements of the present banking system. The Bill seeks to provide a law relating to evidence with respect to bankers’ books and to align it with contemporary digital banking practices. The Bill also has a provision that an electronic or digital record of a banker’s book will be admissible, valid, and legally enforceable as evidence.Replying to discussion on the bill, Finance Minister Sitharaman said that this bill is a very reformative step, which will help the country move forward at a faster pace. She highlighted that the Bankers’ Books Evidence Act was framed in 1891, when banking systems were entirely paper-based. Mrs Sitharaman said, today, India has demonstrated remarkable progress in digitising its economy. She said, banking and financial transactions are now largely driven by digital platforms, often accessible through a simple click on a mobile phone. The Minister said that in such a scenario, it is imperative that the country’s legal framework evolves to keep pace with these advancements. She noted that the existing 1891 Act relies heavily on certified copies of physical bank records as admissible evidence in legal proceedings. Mr Sitharaman said that the Bill establishes a technology-neutral legal framework for bankers’ records, which formally recognises electronic and digital banking records and ensures their admissibility in legal proceedings. It also standardises the certification process and allows authentication through manual, digital, and electronic signatures.Earlier, participating in the discussion, Arun Singh of BJP said that new legislation has been brought to change old act framed in 1891 under British rule. Mr Singh said, this bill will further boost the banking system, which is considered as the backbone of the Indian economy. He said, a revolutionary transformation is being witnessed in the banking system under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Mr Singh said, the bill has the provision that evidences in the digital or computerised form will be accepted as part of evidence.Manas Ranjan Mangaraj of BJD supported the objectives of the bill. He said, data security and privacy must be given the highest priority. He said, as the banking records contain sensitive personal and financial information, the government must ensure strong safeguards to prevent misuse, unauthorized access and cyber threats. Other members also spoke on the bill

. Indian shuttler Ashmita Chaliha produced a superb comeback to win the Korea Masters 2026, beating China’s Han Qian Xi in the women’s singles final this morning. The Assam shuttler recovered from losing the opening game to prevail 14-21, 21-14, and 21-14 in 53 minutes and claim her first BWF title. Earlier, Ashmita reached the final after defeating fellow Indian Rakshitha Ramraj 21-13, 16-21, 21-13 in the semifinal yesterday. While Han outplayed South Korea’s G Kim 22-20, 18-21, and 21-14 in the other semifinal to advance to the final. Ashmita Chaliha had won the gold medal at the 2024 Asia Team Championships. At the 2019 South Asian Games, she had secured gold medals in both the women’s singles and team events.

India’s urban unemployment rate (UR) for persons aged 15 years and above rose marginally to 6.7 per cent during the April to June quarter of current fiscal year, from 6.6 per cent in the previous quarter. According to Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) periodic labour force survey quarterly bulletin, unemployment rate in rural areas increased to 4.8 per cent from 4.3 per cent during the fourth quarter of last fiscal year. Meanwhile, the female urban UR decreased to 8.7 per cent in the current quarter from 9.1 per cent in the last quarter.The data showed that sectoral distribution of employment continued to exhibit similar structural pattern, with the rural workforce predominantly engaged in the primary sector and the urban workforce concentrated in the tertiary sector. The share of regular wage or salaried employees among persons aged 15 years and above increased from 15.5 per cent to 16.1 per cent in rural areas and from 48.9 per cent to 49.3 per cent in urban areas on a sequential basis.The overall Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) among persons of age 15 years and above stood at 54.6 per cent in the first quarter, compared to 55.5 per cent in the previous quarter. In rural areas, LFPR stood at 56.9 per cent, down from 58.2 per cent in fourth quarter of last fiscal. Urban LFPR for the same age group remained unchanged at 50.2 per cent.

. India’s medal tally rises to three at the World Athletics Under-20 Championships in the United States. India’s Basant Kumar Meghwal wins a silver in the high jump, while Shahnavaz Khan wins a bronze in the long jump today. In the men’s high jump, 19-year-old Meghwal cleared his personal best of 2.21 metres to win a silver medal. He became the first Indian to win a medal in the high jump at the World U-20 Championships. Algeria’s Younes Ayachi won the gold, while Great Britain’s Otis Poole took the bronze.In the men’s long jump, Shahnavaz clinched bronze with a best effort of 7.84 metres. The 18-year-old produced his best jump in his third attempt. Italy’s Daniele Inzoli won the gold medal with a jump of 7.97 metres, while Australia’s Mason McGroder took silver with a personal best of 7.96 metres. Earlier, in the javelin throw, Ashish Yadav won silver and became the second Indian after Neeraj Chopra to win at the World Athletics U20 Championships. Yadav produced his best throw of 74.09 metres in the third round yesterday.

Union Minister of Electronics and Information Technology Ashwini Vaishnaw has said that the Government is cognizant of the risks associated with children’s online activities, including exposure to harmful content, cyberbullying, online exploitation and digital addiction.In a written reply to a question in Lok Sabha today, Mr Vaishnaw said that the Government keeps itself informed of global developments and evolving international regulatory approaches relating to online safety, including measures adopted by different jurisdictions for protection of children in the digital environment. He said that the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (DPDP Act) has been enacted, which establishes the legal framework to regulate the processing of digital personal data.The DPDP Act provides a legal framework for safeguarding children’s privacy online. Mr Vaishnaw said that the Ministry is implementing a project on Information Security Education and Awareness for generating human resources in Information Security and creating general awareness on various aspects of cyber hygiene & cyber security among the masses.

Indonesia intensified efforts to combat wildfires that have burned more than 107,000 hectares, deploying hundreds of firefighters and helicopters as blazes spread across the country during an unusually dry season.The largest fire is burning in Bromo Tengger Semeru National Park in East Java, where about 743 hectares have been scorched. Authorities closed the popular tourist destination, including areas around Mount Bromo, until further notice. No injuries or evacuations have been reported.Indonesia’s Coordinating Minister for Political and Security Affairs Djamari Chaniago said cloud-seeding operations were unlikely to be possible through 18th of August because there were no suitable rain-bearing clouds. Firefighters are instead relying on water bombing and ground crews.

. Parliament has passed the Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026, after the Rajya Sabha returned the Money Bill to the Lok Sabha following discussion. The Lok Sabha had earlier passed the Bill, which was then sent to the Rajya Sabha for discussion. Since it is a Money Bill, the Rajya Sabha can only make recommendations on its provisions and return it to the Lok Sabha, which may accept or reject those recommendations.Replying to the discussion on the Bill in the Rajya Sabha, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman made it clear that the legislation does not impose any tax on UPI and that the digital payment system will remain free for consumers.The Finance Minister stated that the UPI-related amendment is only an enabling provision and does not itself impose any tax or transaction charge on users. Ms Sitharaman also said that the government does not intend to impose any MDR charges on small merchants, as they remain central to UPI’s inclusive growth.

The FIH Hockey Men’s and Women’s World Cup 2026 will feature a revamped competition structure, with the traditional quarterfinal stage scrapped and the top two teams from each of the two crossover pools advancing directly to the semi-finals. Belgium and the Netherlands jointly host the tournament from August 15 to 30. The new format means teams will have little margin for error from the outset, with results from the opening pool stage potentially carrying over into the next phase. India’s men have been drawn alongside England, Pakistan and Wales in Pool D, while the Indian women will face China, England and South Africa in their Pool D campaign.The tournament will begin with the 16 teams in each competition split across four pools of four. From August 15 to 20, every team will play three matches against the other sides in its pool, with the final standings determining the composition of the next phase. The top two teams from Pools A and D will move into Pool E, while the leading two teams from Pools B and C will form Pool F. The top two finishers from Pool E and Pool F will advance directly to the last four. The women’s tournament will conclude in the Netherlands on August 29, with the bronze-medal match followed by the final. The men’s World Cup will conclude in Belgium a day later, on August 30, with its bronze-medal match and final.

. Turkey’s Parliament has approved legislation providing for a conditional pardon for thousands of Kurdish militants, as part of the government’s efforts to advance its peace initiative with the Kurdistan Workers’ Party (PKK). The legislation was approved by an overwhelming majority. However, the pardon will come into effect only after Turkish authorities verify that the PKK has fully disarmed.The PKK announced last year that it was ending its decades-long armed campaign against the Turkish state and would dissolve itself as part of the peace process. The decision followed a call by its imprisoned leader, Abdullah Ocalan.The move marks a significant step towards ending a conflict that has claimed tens of thousands of lives. The legislation could also have wider regional implications. It is expected to help strengthen ties between Turkey and Iraq. It could also support efforts by the Syrian government to integrate areas formerly controlled by the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces. Turkey considers the Syrian Democratic Forces affiliated with the PKK.

Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has said that the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) reflects the procurement of the right product of the right quality, at the right price and at the right time. The Minister said this while speaking at the 10th Foundation Day of GeM in New Delhi yesterday.Mr Goyal recalled that prior to the introduction of GeM, public money was being misused, procurement was non-transparent and lacked good governance. He underlined that today, procurement is being carried out through a public procurement e-commerce platform, where transparency, competitiveness and strong standards are maintained before registration.Mr Goyal said GeM is an effort to digitise public procurement and replace opacity with transparency. He noted that since the introduction of the GeM portal, its gross merchandise value has grown to over five lakh crore rupees per year over the last two years, from over four hundred crore rupees in 2016-17.Mr Goyal said cumulatively, GeM has helped in the procurement of over twenty lakh crore rupees worth of goods and services through the portal, through more than three crore orders. He underlined that procurement worth ten lakh crore rupees took place in the first eight years, while the next ten lakh crore rupees was covered in only two years.The Minister mentioned that over 2.25 lakh women-led enterprises have won orders worth nearly one lakh crore rupees through the portal. He added that over 42,000 start-ups have carried out business with government enterprises worth almost 66,000 crore rupees. Mr Goyal informed that GeM is being revamped and a new user-friendly, AI-enabled portal will be launched soon.The Minister also launched a dedicated nationwide five-digit short code, 14550, for the GeM Helpdesk, enabling buyers, sellers and other stakeholders to access support and identify official GeM communications.

. India will host the first Global South Film Festival next year. It was announced today at a press conference held on the sidelines of the BRICS WAVES Bazaar in Mumbai. Several agreements aimed at strengthening international cooperation in the film and entertainment sector were also announced.Organisations including the National Film Development Corporation (NFDC) and the National Film Archive of India (NFAI) signed agreements, exchanged Letters of Intent and held talks with partner institutions from countries including Brazil, Russia and Vietnam. The participating organisations also agreed to explore opportunities for film co-production.The two-day WAVES BRICS Bazaar, which opened in Mumbai yesterday, concludes this evening. Prakash Magdum, Managing Director of the NFDC, said the initiative brought together more than 900 delegates from the 20 BRICS member and partner countries. Around 250 meetings were held during the one-and-a-half-day event, providing a platform for government agencies, entertainment industry professionals, investors and content creators to exchange ideas and explore opportunities for collaboration.
